To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the preclinical phase in IDDM is characterized by a variable rate of beta-cell destruction, and that the rate of beta-cell loss can be predicted from the level of islet-cell autoimmunity.

the development of IDDM in siblings of patients with IDDM is characterized by an early and strong islet-cell-specific autoimmunity, a reduced insulin secreting ability and a progressive impairment in glucose tolerance.

the preclinical phase is long (median 29.5 months) and is characterized by increasing signs of isleta-cell specific autoimmunty, decreasing insulin secreting capacity, and emerging glucose intolerance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preclinical phase in IDDM.
the preclinical phase preceding the clinical onset of IDDM.
the natural history of the preclinical phase and with the identification of the earliest signs of IDDM in high-risk individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the preclinical phase is a variable process in terms of time, autoimmunity and beta-cell function, and is characterized by a gradual deterioration of beta-cell function, which is not constant but rather variable.

the preclinical phase is characterized by the presence of islet cell antibodies, a progressive decline in the insulin secretion rate, a reduction in the insulin secretory capacity, and a reduction in glucose induced insulin secretion.
the natural history of preclinical type 1 diabetes is complex, variable and not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preclinical phase can be characterized as a dynamic process with a variable rate of beta-cell destruction.
we have shown that the preclinical phase in high risk siblings is a period with increasing signs of islets-cell specific autoimmunty and a progressive deterioration of insulin secreting capacity.
preclinical IDDM is characterized by a progressive loss of beta cell function and an increasing level of islet-cell-specific antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are able to identify individuals at risk of developing type 1 diabetes.
there is no single test or combination of tests that is sufficiently sensitive or specific to identify those at risk of developing IDDM.
there is a lot of heterogeneity in the natural history of preclinical type 1 diabetes.
